beats.say: 2.867 days: Algol, the Medusa star, is winking at us this October.
Space.com says this binary star system represents the eye of the Gorgon Medusa in the constellation Perseus.
It appears to dim regularly because one star eclipses the other, creating a spooky, flickering effect in the sky.
If you look towards the constellation Taurus this month, you might also spot Taurid meteors streaking past.
These are often called Halloween fireballs because they coincide perfectly with our annual spooky celebrations.
While you are watching the sky, you can also look for the Pleiades star cluster or the whale constellation Cetus.
The universe has a natural light show ready for your Halloween 2026 countdown. Will you be stargazing this week?

facts: The binary star system Algol represents an eye of the Gorgon Medusa in the constellation Perseus.
The binary star Algol appears to dim every 2.867 days as one star eclipses the other.
Taurid meteors are often called Halloween fireballs because they coincide with the annual celebration.
The Pleiades star cluster is a collection of six or seven bright stars visible to the naked eye.
The constellation Cetus is also known as the sea monster or the whale.
